newsitem.title: UK: Man sees 96/97 world sugar output at 122.80 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Man sees 96/97 world sugar output at 122.80 mln t.

text.p: World 1996/97 (crop year) sugar output will total 122.802 million tonnes, according to a report released by international trade house E D & F Man.
This compares with the previous Man estimate of 122.722 million tonnes and the previous year's output of 123.706 million tonnes. The figures are based on raw value.
Man put the world's 1996/97 sugar surplus at 2.10 million tonnes, compared with an earlier estimate of 2.43 million tonnes and compared with the previous year's surplus of 5.12 million tonnes.
In its latest Sugar Situation report, Man said its estimate for world cane sugar production had been reduced by 249,000 tonnes, while beet showed a 329,000 tonne increase.

The reduction for cane was due to cuts for a number of leading producers, including Cuba, India and Thailand, Man said. "However, the reduction has been limited by a range of upward adjustments for the central American sugar producers where record crops are being witnessed more or less across the board this sseason," Man said.
The upward adjustment for beet was due to better than expected crops in China and the US, along with a record UK beet crop, Man said.
